correctness.rationale: Independent reproduction computed exact integer binomial sums at each of 19 odd primes through 71 and t=3,4,5 (57 cases). All sums are zero modulo p² and have nonzero residues modulo p⁴. Normalized residues give valuation 2 except at 7 and 71, where the p³ units are respectively 1 mod 7 and 5 mod 71 for all three truncations. To extend to every t>=5, write A_t-A_5=p^5 h with h a nonnegative integer. For 1<=j<=K<p², the identity j*binom(p^5 h,j)=p^5 h*binom(p^5 h-1,j-1) puts every j>0 Vandermonde term at 0 mod p⁴; the zero shift is trivial. Thus the nonzero residues mod p⁴ certify exact orders and nonzero S at every t>=3, not just sampled t. At t=2 complementary binomial terms cancel, so it must remain excluded. The repaired RESULT.md qualifies the nonliteral zero-digit specialization of González and supplies the correct prior implication from Ichino–Prasanna: the same Vandermonde polynomial identity at the p-adic shift p^t/2, with p-integrality of each binomial polynomial and v_p(j)<=1, transfers the p² layer from -1/2 to A_t. No theorem, range, or residue was changed. Replay: /workspace/branches/e388a124-0a48-4ac4-b16f-a293c5ef6921/{check_record3.py,check_record3.out}. The supplied verifier was inspected, not executed.

evidence: Theorem 3.1 plus the shift p^t/2 gives the generic lower bound at all t>=3 but no upper bound on valuation.

For p>=5, set X=2^(p−1)=1+p q, B=(p−1)/2, H=(p²−1)/2 and let C_K=binom(−1/2,K). Morley gives C_B≡X mod p³. Jacobsthal scaling of binom(p(p−1),pB) gives C_(pB)≡X^(2−p). In the product for (−1)^H binom(p²−1,H), the factors at multiples of p give X² by Morley, and the others give 1−p² H_B since complete residue blocks have reciprocal sum zero mod p. Dividing by 4^H gives C_H≡X^(1−p)(1−p² H_B). Hence the p-adic sum is p²(q²−2q) mod p³, using H_B≡−2q mod p. To transfer this layer at t=3, in the signed Vandermonde expansion only j=pr>0 can contribute mod p³; the two surviving coefficients at lower indices p(B−r) and p(B−r)+B agree mod p by Lucas (lowest digit of −1/2 is B). For t>=4 the transfer is immediate. The p=3 residue is directly checked.

value.rationale: The valuation invariant tests the sharpness of a known digit-depth supercongruence on its smallest nontrivial four-term slice. The bound 71 is the point at which the second exception is attained, not a claim about an arbitrary range of primes. The computations distinguish ordinary sharpness, extra cancellation and exact termination at the next p-adic digit at both exceptional primes; the answer holds for every eligible truncation rather than just small input binomial coefficients. Even recognizing the equivalent Fermat-quotient test for extra divisibility does not supply these exact exceptional orders.
